Congrats to Gemini 4 Hydrogen on their launch and it seems Anthropic’s IPO is well under way, but today’s headline was only ever going to be about one thing, the most earthshaking leadership change in AI (after Demis/Jeff/et al at Google DeepMind).

Yesterday we covered reports that NVIDIA’s board was preparing to replace Jensen Huang following an NYT report of an affair with an accused Chinese spy. Following news of a second affair, today NVIDIA announced his resignation (correlation/causation is debatable here), presumably forced by the board:

View post on X ↗

There is also some discussion of the extent that Chinese models can demonstrably be shown to be trained on Blackwell GPUs that they should not have access to… though the scale is debated.

After 33 years, Jensen Huang has stepped down as CEO, president and boardmember. Colette Kress, NVIDIA’s CFO since 2013, will keep that job while serving as interim CEO… leading into what will presumably the best attended earnings call in the history of $NVDA next week.

AI News for 11/11/2026-11/12/2026. We checked 12 subreddits, 544 Twitters and no further Discords. AINews' website lets you search all past issues. As a reminder, AINews is now a section of Latent Space. You can opt in/out of email frequencies!

Gemini 4 Hydrogen: Google's Fast Gemini 4 Tier Ships Broadly

Google says it completes tasks 2.5x faster than Gemini 3.8 Flash and edges Argon on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, 51 vs 50 at default thinking and 54 at the new xhigh level (DeepMind, Koray Kavukcuoglu).

Specs and pricing: The model offers four thinking levels (low, medium, high and xhigh) and a 1M context window. It costs $1.50/$7.50 per million input/output tokens, with a 95% discount on cached input (Phil Schmid, Artificial Analysis).

Official claims: Google reports 57% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 and more than 3x Gemini 3.8 Flash on Terminal-Bench 4.1. It also claims more than 5x fewer fabricated claims, #1 on Vals Tax Agent Bench and leading results on AutomationBench-AA and Agents' Last Exam (Google).

Availability: Hydrogen is available on all Gemini API tiers, including a free tier in AI Studio. It is the default model in Search AI Mode, and free Gemini app users get it through auto-selection. Paid Pro and Ultra subscribers can use it in Antigravity (Sundar Pichai, GeminiApp, Search).

kandidaty.tekst:
Release: llm-gemini 0.37

Google launched Gemini 4 Hydrogen today - the lowest cost member of the Gemini 4 family.

It's actually not too far off the price of its much bigger siblings, Carbon and Argon. I'm finding Gemini 4's pricing really confusing. Here's the pricing scheme:

Carbon and Argon are the same price, and both are scheduled to double in price on December 1st. If they're the same price, why have two different models? Google says that Argon "delivers Gemini 4 intelligence with faster responses and lower token spend per turn compared to Gemini 4 Carbon" - so it may be priced the same, but it will use less tokens per task.

Hydrogen, supposedly the cheap model, is currently only a 25% discount on its more capable peers. The Hydrogen price will make more sense after December 1st, when it will represent a 75% discount. It's still considerably more expensive than Claude Haiku 5.5 and GPT-6 Luna - they're both $0.10/$0.50, so Hydrogen is 15x that.

I had Hydrogen generate some pelicans. Here's a full comparison grid showing the pelicans for all three members of the Gemini 4 family at their three supported effort levels:

Considering how close they are in price, the difference in pelican quality for Hydrogen is quite stark.

Here's how Google describe Hydrogen's intended position in their mix of models:

In real-world software development, while teams rely on frontier models like Carbon and Argon for deep architectural judgment when designing systems or untangling subtle bugs, they still need a fast, disciplined execution model for writing code, running tests, and verifying changes. Hydrogen is built to stand on its own as a model for everyday work — or to pair with Carbon and Argon as the high-efficiency execution engine in multi-model workflows.

Most notably, Hydrogen is the new free tier model, and is the model that will power AI features in Google Search.

kandidaty.zagolovok: To the man with AI, everything looks like a task
kandidaty.tekst:
Now I’m having fun!

My Ramp post was really well received with one or two ‘I’m not sure what I just looked at’ comments (which is totally fair).

The best I can describe what I’m doing now is exploring people and companies who are having fun with AI, doing things differently, being authentic and succeeding.

Which is basically how I want to describe my ‘work’.

But I think a lot of people are living in fear. Scared they’re behind, they’re not doing enough, others using AI ‘better’ than them, where’s there job going etc.

I want to focus on using AI for fun.

AI is a tool, you need one agent app (I’ve been using Droid with Opus 5.5 medium, fast mode for my posts, fable here and there). Use the tool to do work beyond what you could do before, don’t think about how you can finally optimise every aspect of every little thing. (I’ve basically stopped using Grok Bot, except telling me when the tennis is on).

As part of my explorations I’m working on a new post for another company I admire and who do things very differently. Coming next week…

“Everyone judges a book by its cover”

Can you guess which company it is?

And yes, these animations are staying. Honestly I love them. I love making them too.

So much so that I set up a sophisticated camera set up to monitor what my days look like and here’s the footage.

Morning voice dump. Kids. Stickmen.

kandidaty.tekst: Agent Anomaly Detection (AAD) provides asynchronous, low-latency monitoring for AI agents by analyzing OpenTelemetry traces and logs to flag goal hijacks and tool misuse. Developers can integrate AAD alongside semantic governance and strict tool limits as part of a defense-in-depth strategy to secure agentic applications.

kandidaty.tekst:
@testingcatalog: Retell crossed a $100M revenue run rate and introduced Tell 1, its first AI model designed to power the voice agents used in enterprise contact centers.

According to Retell, Tell 1 was trained on more than 1 million hours of customer calls, which allows it to reason through complex requests without making the caller wait.

Retell users can also use Conductor, a tool that analyzes failed calls, creates test cases, and proposes fixes for approval.

Цитирует @_bingwu: Retell just crossed $100M in revenue run rate.

$10M to $100M in 17 months. Profitable. $4.6M raised.

From day one, we’ve focused on solving the hardest parts of deploying voice AI in the product itself, so customers can build, manage, and improve their own agents without depending on us.

Our bet: the future of the contact center belongs to the teams who run it.

Proud of our team. Grateful to every customer who believed in us.

The next billion computers?

With box, agents open apps, run the terminal, fill in forms, and stay signed in for whatever tasks come next.

Users can then approve a change, ship it, and have Wave measure how well the fix worked.

A full-stack product owner 👀

Цитирует @spenserskates: Introducing Wave.

The world's first AI that reads your customers' mind.

$1.47 trillion will be spent on software this year, but only a fraction of software features are used by customers.

AI can build anything you want, but it doesn't know what your customers need.

Wave fixes that.
